name: Soybean
desc: A common Kharif pulse-oilseed option in suitable regions.
risks: Sensitive to waterlogging; verify local variety and sowing timing.
tip: Check local sowing recommendations with your district agriculture office.

tasks: Prepare a fine seedbed with good drainage.
Use certified seed of a locally recommended variety; treat seed with Rhizobium culture.
Sow at recommended spacing once soil moisture is adequate.
Check germination and fill gaps within the first fortnight.
Protect seedlings from heavy rain crusting; drain excess water quickly.
One hand weeding around 20–25 days (or as per local advice).
Keep the field free of the first flush of weeds.
Avoid moisture stress during flowering; irrigate only if the crop is rain-fed and dry.
Do not disturb the crop; support with locally approved plant-protection only if pests cross threshold.
Monitor for defoliator and girdle beetle activity as per local advisories.
Ensure drainage; soybean suffers badly in waterlogging.
Harvest when pods dry and leaves drop.
Dry and thresh promptly to avoid shattering losses.

name: Pearl millet (Bajra)
desc: A hardy grain crop option in suitable warm regions.
risks: Yield depends on rainfall timing and variety.

tasks: Sow with the first effective monsoon showers on a fine seedbed.
Use certified seed of a drought-tolerant local variety.
Thin to one healthy plant per hill and fill gaps within two weeks.
Complete inter-cultivation and hand weeding.
Apply nitrogen top dressing only as per soil-test-based local advice.
Protect from moisture stress at boot stage if rain fails.
Watch for ergot/downy mildew symptoms; consult local advisory before any spray.
Protect ripening ears from birds.
Avoid excess moisture; drain waterlogged patches.
Harvest earheads when grains are hard; dry before threshing.
Store fodder for livestock use.

name: Sorghum (Jowar)
desc: A versatile grain and fodder crop used in rain-fed farming systems.
risks: Season and variety selection differ by region.
tip: Check region-specific guidance and soil moisture.

tasks: Sow on a prepared seedbed with adequate moisture.
Keep recommended row spacing for inter-cultivation.
Thin and gap-fill within two to three weeks of emergence.
Apply split nitrogen doses only as per local soil-test advice.
Complete weeding before the crop closes canopy.
Watch for shoot fly and stem borer; follow local integrated-pest advice.
Irrigate if available during long dry spells.
Protect from birds; drain excess water in Kharif.
Harvest grain at physiological maturity; cut fodder at the right stage.
Plan fodder storage or marketing along with grain.

name: Groundnut
desc: Can suit well-drained soils with a suitable rainfall pattern.
tip: Confirm drainage and local disease advice.

tasks: Sow well-filled kernels of a local recommended variety on a loose seedbed.
Ensure the field drains quickly; avoid low patches.
Complete first weeding before pegging begins.
Keep soil loose around plants so pegs can enter; apply gypsum only as per local advice.
Do not disturb the soil once pegging starts.
Maintain even moisture; avoid alternate wet-dry cycles.
Monitor for leaf miner and tikka disease per local advisories.
Scratch-test pods: dark inside-shell markings indicate maturity.
Lift, shake off soil and dry pods in shade first, then sun.
Store dry pods below 8–9% moisture to avoid aflatoxin risk.

name: Maize
desc: A multi-season crop where water and local markets are suitable.
risks: Water needs rise at flowering and grain filling.
tip: Check local water availability and buyer access.

tasks: Sow certified seed at recommended spacing and depth.
Plan market/buyer link before choosing grain vs. green-cob vs. fodder type.
Thin to one plant per hill; fill gaps within 10 days.
Apply first nitrogen top dressing as per local soil-test advice.
Earthing-up after top dressing helps stand the crop.
Maize needs the most water from knee-high to grain filling; irrigate if dry.
Scout weekly for fall armyworm; follow local IPM guidance.
Maintain moisture; avoid stress which cuts grain size.
Harvest when husk dries and grains show black layer.
Dry cobs to safe moisture before shelling and storage.

name: Rice (Paddy)
desc: A crop for suitable lowland or irrigated conditions.

tasks: Raise nursery with certified seed of a locally recommended variety.
Transplant 20–25 day seedlings at recommended spacing in puddled field.
Maintain thin standing water after transplanting.
Apply nitrogen in splits as per local advice; complete weeding.
Keep water 2–5 cm deep; do not let the field crack.
Apply final nitrogen top dressing per local recommendation.
Watch for stem borer and leaf folder; follow local advisories.
Never let the crop stress at flowering; keep shallow water.
Avoid pesticide sprays during peak flowering hours to protect bees.
Drain the field gradually near maturity as per local practice.
Harvest at 20–25% grain moisture; dry to 14% before storage.
Plan straw management; avoid burning where restricted.

name: Cotton
desc: A region-specific cash crop associated with suitable soils and a long season.
risks: Long duration, pests and input costs create risk.
tip: Review local pest-management and seed guidance.

tasks: Sow certified seed after soil warms and monsoon settles.
Use recommended spacing; deep black soils suit this deep-rooted crop.
Thin to recommended plant population; fill gaps early.
Apply balanced nutrition per soil-test advice; avoid excess nitrogen.
Install traps/pheromone lures as per local pest-management guidance.
Scout twice weekly for pink bollworm and sucking pests; act only on thresholds.
Avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum sprays; protect natural enemies.
Pick clean, dry kapas in 2–3 rounds; keep grades separate.
Moist kapas spoils quality — never pick wet bolls.
Remove and destroy stalks to break pest cycles before next season.
Plan soil test after long-duration crop.

name: Chickpea (Chana)
desc: A Rabi pulse option with suitable residual moisture.
risks: Excess moisture and disease pressure may affect the crop.
tip: Check soil moisture and local disease precautions.

tasks: Sow on residual moisture with a locally recommended variety.
Seed treatment per local advice; avoid sowing too deep.
Nipping (top clipping) as practiced locally may improve branching.
Keep field weed-free; one hand weeding around 25–30 days.
Scout for pod borer (Helicoverpa) weekly; use local IPM advice — pheromone traps, bird perches.
One light irrigation at flowering/branching if available.
Avoid excess water; chickpea fails more often from moisture than drought.
Harvest when pods dry and plants turn straw-coloured.
Dry to safe moisture before threshing and storage.

name: Wheat
desc: Can suit Rabi conditions where temperature, soil and irrigation match.
risks: Heat during grain filling and limited irrigation affect yields.
tip: Verify regional suitability and sowing date.

tasks: Sow a locally recommended variety in the correct window; late sowing costs yield.
Use seed rate per local advice; place fertilizer as recommended.
First irrigation around 20–25 days is the most critical one.
Apply first nitrogen top dressing before or with this irrigation.
Second irrigation; keep weeds in check (weed-free first 40 days matter most).
Third irrigation; watch for yellow rust alerts in your district.
Never skip irrigation at booting.
Protect from terminal heat; evening irrigation can help if heat wave is forecast.
Monitor for rust and aphid as per local advisories.
Harvest when grain is hard and straw golden; combine or manual as available.
Dry grain to 12% moisture for storage.

name: Mustard
desc: An oilseed option in selected Rabi regions.
tip: Check whether mustard is recommended in your district.

tasks: Sow in the recommended Rabi window with proper seed rate.
Keep rows spaced for inter-cultivation.
Thin to keep healthy plants; remove excess seedlings.
First irrigation at rosette stage (~30 days) with nitrogen top dressing as per advice.
Watch aphid clusters on shoots; use local IPM thresholds before spraying.
Protect bees — mustard depends on pollination.
Second irrigation at siliqua filling if needed; avoid over-watering.
Harvest when 75% siliquae turn yellow-brown; avoid shattering.
Dry and thresh; store oilseed in dry conditions.

name: Onion
desc: A higher-management horticulture option where drainage and markets suit.
risks: Price swings, storage and disease can substantially affect returns.
tip: Check local prices, storage and crop-protection costs.

tasks: Transplant 6–8 week nursery seedlings on raised beds with good drainage.
Plan storage and market link before committing area — onion is price-volatile.
Light, frequent irrigation; onion roots are shallow.
Top dressing per soil-test advice; keep beds weed-free.
Maintain even moisture; stress now splits or doubles bulbs.
Monitor thrips weekly; follow local plant-protection advice.
Continue light irrigation; do not overwater near maturity.
Purple blotch/alternaria watch — act per local advisory only.
Stop irrigation when 50–70% tops fall over.
Lift, cure bulbs in shade with tops for 2–3 weeks where suitable.
Sort and grade before storage or sale; diseased bulbs must be removed.

name: Green gram (Moong)
desc: A relatively short-duration pulse for locally suitable windows.
risks: Sensitive to sowing window, pests and rainfall distribution.
tip: Confirm local variety, timing and demand.

tasks: Sow a locally recommended short-duration variety; precise window matters.
One weeding around 20 days keeps the fast crop clean.
Avoid moisture stress at flowering if irrigating; rain-fed crops depend on timely showers.
Watch whitefly/jassids and pod borers; follow local IPM advice.
Avoid sprays close to harvest.
Pick mature pods in 1–2 rounds; dry and thresh promptly.
Short duration frees the field for the next crop — plan rotation.

name: Sugarcane
desc: A long-duration crop grown in suitable irrigated districts with access to a mill.
risks: High water, capital and market-access requirements; not suitable for every farm.
tip: Verify water allocation, planting window and mill access locally.

tasks: Plant healthy setts of an approved variety in the district planting window.
Ensure assured irrigation and a mill/gur market link BEFORE planting.
Fill gaps and complete first top dressing per local advice.
Begin inter-cultivation and earthing-up as canes grow.
Peak water demand — schedule irrigation strictly per local guidance.
Split nitrogen applications as per soil-test-based advice.
Continue irrigation; propping/tying prevents lodging in wind.
Monitor for borers and wilt per local advisories.
Reduce irrigation near maturity as advised; sucrose accumulates best in dry, clear weather.
Harvest per mill slip/calendar; strip and deliver promptly — delays cut weight and quality.
Plan ratoon management or rotation after harvest.
